headline: Meta, Walmart, Stripe and the AI company Sierra are creating a shared standard, called the Personal Agent Protocol, for how people's AI agents deal with businesses online.
score_reason: Several outlets and a Sierra co-founder blog post support the plan, but it is a proposed open standard with no stated adoption yet; score kept.
importance_line: Shoppers who send AI agents to buy for them and the stores those agents visit would get common rules for identity and visibility, but the standard is new and its safety claims are untested.
summary: SiliconANGLE reports, citing interviews first given to CNBC, that Meta is working with Walmart, Stripe and the enterprise AI firm Sierra on the Personal Agent Protocol, which is meant to let businesses tell authorised AI agents apart and see what personal agents do on their websites. Sierra co-founder Bret Taylor, who also chairs OpenAI Group, says there "will be chaos until such a standard exists" and expects OpenAI to back it later; SiliconANGLE says the move appears to answer a call by six major banks for standards on AI agents.
notes: CNBC page returned 403; text read at SiliconANGLE (6 Oct 2026), which cites CNBC interviews. The url is the original CNBC article from the pool. Muse security and privacy criticism is background in SiliconANGLE, not reported by us.
